purpose: Attribution correction audit: preserves v1.1 registered records alongside v1.2 corrected assessments

corrections.Q08: v1.1 classified operational falsification machinery as 'exploratory_findings' (an empirical status); v1.2 separates research-method implementation from scientific findings -> insufficient_evidence
corrections.Q11: v1.1 labelled the broad debt-burden claim inconsistent based on one public-debt operationalization; v1.2 scopes the negative result to the tested proposition (5y public debtgdp change) -> evaluated_with_no_clear_conclusion
corrections.Q14: v1.1 status inherited from a change-based protocol that never tested level thresholds; v1.2 uses dedicated H01T-P1.0 level-threshold diagnostics -> evaluated_with_no_clear_conclusion
corrections.Q17: v1.1 inherited contradictory status from a PUBLIC-debt protocol (attribution defect); v1.2 separates the public-debt experiment from the private-credit H01B-P1.0 exploratory diagnostic -> exploratory_findings

validation-questions-v1.1.current_answer: The falsification machinery exists, but only H01 has an evaluated result.

validation-questions-v1.2.current_answer: Research method is implemented (registered falsification criteria, append-only evaluations preserving negative results); H01-P1.0 and H01B-P1.0 have been executed. But a scientific answer to WHICH observations support or falsify the theory requires populated independent outcome registries beyond one banking-crisis family — operational machinery alone is not an empirical finding.

validation-questions-v1.1.current_answer: H01-P1.0 found no predictive value in 5-year public-debt/GDP growth before banking crises (AUC 0.30-0.38); public and private debt behave differently around banking crises.

validation-questions-v1.2.current_answer: Scoped correction (v1.2): the registered H01-P1.0 test contradicted one specific operationalized proposition — 5-year PUBLIC debt/GDP change as a crisis predictor (AUC 0.363/0.381/0.296). That negative result does not falsify the broader debt-cycle claim: H01B-P1.0 found positive retrospective discrimination for PRIVATE credit expansion (tloans/gdp 5y change AUC 0.719, income-residualised 0.717), and public debt characteristically surges AFTER crises via bailouts and automatic stabilisers. The broad registered claim remains only partially tested.

validation-questions-v1.1.current_answer: Neither public-debt changes nor historical debt-to-GDP level percentiles provide a reproducible out-of-sample crisis threshold.

validation-questions-v1.2.current_answer: H01T-P1.0 evaluated level thresholds directly: no reproducible UNIVERSAL debt-to-GDP crisis threshold exists — pooled p80 levels discriminate at/below chance for public debt and over-flag for private credit, while per-country thresholds differ by ~5x. Thresholds appear conditional on country, era and monetary regime; that heterogeneity, not a single cutoff, is the supported research direction.

validation-questions-v1.1.current_answer: Preserved contradictory H01-P1.0 benchmark reflects a variable mismatch (public debtgdp was tested instead of private tloans/gdp); exploratory tloans/gdp shows positive retrospective association but awaits an independent pre-registered protocol.

validation-questions-v1.2.current_answer: Attribution corrected: H01-P1.0's negative result applies only to public debt. Under dedicated protocol H01B-P1.0, private-credit expansion shows positive retrospective association with banking-crisis onset that survives income-growth residualisation and clustered diagnostics — classified exploratory because the holdout is no longer untouched and only 3 independent episodes remain.
